newsitem.title: UK: Britain urges France to let British drivers return.
newsitem.headline: Britain urges France to let British drivers return.

text.p: British Transport Secretary Sir George Young pleaded on Wednesday for the release of British drivers blockaded in France by striking French truckers.
In a letter to French Transport Minister Bernard Pons, Young said the British drivers were innocent victims of the dispute which has dragged on for more than week.
"I must stress how very urgent it now is to secure the release of all those British lorries which are still detained," said Young.
"British drivers have nothing to do with this dispute, and there is a growing sense of anger in Britain that so many still remain trapped."
Talks between French truckers and employers broke down without agreement late on Wednesday, said a senior trade union official.
Unions are maintaining about 250 roadblocks on France's highways.

The roadblocks have forced fuel rationing in some areas, closed some factories and cut supplies of perishable goods ranging from fish to fruit. Several British supermarkets have started airlifts of fresh fruit and vegetables to ensure a steady supply.

Thousands of drivers from Britain, Spain, Germany and other countries have been trapped by the blockades without enough food or money. Growing tensions have sometimes caused violent confrontations with French truckers.
Young said it was time to get the British drivers out.
"Many British businesses have suffered serious losses because vehicles and drivers have been prevented from conducting their normal business," he wrote.
